claim: Compressed Perturb-seq was reported to use composite perturbation measurements and sparse recovery to reduce experimental cost while retaining single-perturbation and second-order interaction information in a human macrophage model.
future_grounding_route: Use only as design context until a project-specific pilot prospectively compares compressed and conventional measurements with held-out perturbations and prespecified recovery error.
project_use: External feasibility context for testing perturbation combinations without treating model compression as evidence.
relationship_note: The method offers a way to test interactions more efficiently, but its assumptions and accuracy have not been validated in an MS-relevant human CNS model by this project.

source.citation: Cleary et al. Scalable genetic screening for regulatory circuits using compressed Perturb-seq. Nature Biotechnology. 2024.
source.label: Compressed Perturb-seq

source_terms.license_or_terms_label: Publisher page metadata and short paraphrase only
source_terms.reuse_notes: Store bibliographic metadata and a short paraphrase; do not redistribute article text.

why_unverifiable: The project has not reproduced the compressed screen or validated sparse recovery in an MS-relevant model.
